kb_knowledge.text:
Symptoms

Web pages fail to load with "DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN" or "Server not found" errors. Applications report hostname resolution failures. The command nslookup returns "Non-existent domain."

Cause

DNS failures can result from misconfigured DNS server addresses, DNS server outage, corrupted local DNS cache, DHCP not assigning DNS servers, or network adapter misconfiguration.

Resolution

  1. Flush the DNS resolver cache: ipconfig /flushdns (Windows) or sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder (Mac).
  2. Verify DNS server settings: ipconfig /all and check DNS Servers listed.
  3. Test with a public DNS server: temporarily set DNS to 8.8.8.8 (Google) or 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare).
  4. Release and renew IP configuration: ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew.
  5. Check if the DNS service is running on the server: nslookup hostname dns-server-ip.

Workaround

Add critical hostname-to-IP mappings to the local hosts file (C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts) as a temporary measure while DNS is being restored.

Verification

  1. Run nslookup company-domain.com and confirm it returns the correct IP address.
  2. Open a browser and navigate to an internal website by hostname.
  3. Verify that ping hostname resolves correctly.
